<div id="a14516" style="position:absolute;font-size:14.08px;left:96.032px;top:16.8px;">&#160;</div><div id="a14517" style="position:absolute;left:401.347px;top:1012.3px;">33 </div><div id="a14519" dramatically in 2020 with<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.05px">&#160;</div>simultaneous demand and supply shocks that drove </div><div id="a14553" style="position:absolute;font-size:14.08px;left:96.032px;top:144.5px;">the industry into a severe downturn.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5.96px">&#160;</div>The demand shock was triggered by COVID-19,<div style="display:inline-block;width:1.93px">&#160;</div>which was declared a </div><div id="a14589" style="position:absolute;font-size:14.08px;left:96.032px;top:160.6px;">global pandemic and caused unprecedented social<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.14px">&#160;</div>and economic consequences.<div style="display:inline-block;width:6.12px">&#160;</div>Mitigation efforts to stop the </div><div id="a14617" style="position:absolute;font-size:14.08px;left:96.032px;top:176.8px;">spread of this contagious disease included stay-at-home<div style="display:inline-block;width:1.81px">&#160;</div>orders and business closures that caused sharp </div><div id="a14649" style="position:absolute;font-size:14.08px;left:96.032px;top:192.8px;">contractions in economic activity worldwide.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5.81px">&#160;</div>The supply shock was triggered by disagreements<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.04px">&#160;</div>between </div><div id="a14676" style="position:absolute;font-size:14.08px;left:96.032px;top:208.9px;">OPEC and Russia, beginning in early March, which<div style="display:inline-block;width:2px">&#160;</div>resulted in significant supply coming onto the market<div style="display:inline-block;width:1.92px">&#160;</div>and </div><div id="a14710" style="position:absolute;font-size:14.08px;left:96.032px;top:225.1px;">an oil price war.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7.37px">&#160;</div>These dual demand and supply shocks caused<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.16px">&#160;</div>oil prices to collapse as we exited the first </div><div id="a14750" style="position:absolute;font-size:14.08px;left:96.032px;top:241.1px;">quarter. </div><div id="a14752" style="position:absolute;font-size:14.08px;left:96.032px;top:257.3px;">&#160;</div><div id="a14753" style="position:absolute;font-size:14.08px;left:96.032px;top:273.3px;">As we entered the second quarter, predictions of COVID-19 driven global<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.1px">&#160;</div>oil demand losses intensified, with </div><div id="a14787" style="position:absolute;font-size:14.08px;left:96.032px;top:289.4px;">forecasts of unprecedented demand declines.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5.64px">&#160;</div>Based on these forecasts, OPEC plus nations held<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.16px">&#160;</div>an emergency </div><div id="a14817" style="position:absolute;font-size:14.08px;left:96.032px;top:305.6px;">meeting, and in April they announced a coordinated<div style="display:inline-block;width:1.98px">&#160;</div>production cut that was unprecedented in both its </div><div id="a14850" style="position:absolute;font-size:14.08px;left:96.032px;top:321.6px;">magnitude and duration.<div style="display:inline-block;width:6.27px">&#160;</div>The OPEC plus agreement spans from May 2020<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.18px">&#160;</div>until April 2022, with the volume </div><div id="a14885" style="position:absolute;font-size:14.08px;left:96.032px;top:337.8px;">of production cuts easing over time.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5.97px">&#160;</div>Additionally, non-OPEC plus countries, including the U.S., Canada, </div><div id="a14917" style="position:absolute;font-size:14.08px;left:96.032px;top:353.8px;">Brazil and other G-20 countries, announced organic reductions<div style="display:inline-block;width:1.77px">&#160;</div>to production through the release of drilling </div><div id="a14949" style="position:absolute;font-size:14.08px;left:96.032px;top:369.9px;">rigs, frac crews, normal field decline and curtailments.<div       id="ID_979">Certain of our derivative instruments contain provisions that require us to post collateral if the derivative exposure exceeds a threshold amount.  We have contracts with fixed threshold amounts and other contracts with variable threshold amounts that are contingent on our credit rating.  The variable threshold amounts typically decline for lower credit ratings, while both the variable and fixed threshold amounts typically revert to zero if we fall below investment grade.  Cash is the primary collateral in all contracts; however, many also permit us to post letters of credit as collateral, such as transactions administered through the New York Mercantile Exchange.</us-gaap:CreditDerivativeRecourseProvisions>

<table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" class="authRefData" style="display: none;" id="defref_us-gaap_ExplorationExpense">
<tr><td class="hide"><a style="color: white;" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.hideAR();">X</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>Exploration expenses (including prospecting) related to oil and gas producing entities and would be included in operating expenses of that entity. Costs incurred in identifying areas that may warrant examination and in examining specific areas that are considered to have prospects of containing oil and gas reserves, including costs of drilling exploratory wells and exploratory-type stratigraphic test wells. Exploration costs may be incurred both before acquiring the related property (sometimes referred to in part as prospecting costs) and after acquiring the property. Principal types of exploration costs, which include depreciation and applicable operating costs of support equipment and facilities and other costs of exploration activities, are: (i) Costs of topographical, geographical and geophysical studies, rights of access to properties to conduct those studies, and salaries and other expenses of geologists, geophysical crews, and others conducting those studies. Collectively, these are sometimes referred to as geological and geophysical or "G&amp;G" costs. (ii) Costs of carrying and retaining undeveloped properties, such as delay rentals, ad valorem taxes on properties, legal costs for title defense, and the maintenance of land and lease records. (iii) Dry hole contributions and bottom hole contributions. (iv) Costs of drilling and equipping exploratory wells. (v) Costs of drilling exploratory-type stratigraphic test wells.</p></div>

<tr><td class="hide"><a style="color: white;" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.hideAR();">X</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>The aggregate total costs related to selling a firm's product and services, as well as all other general and administrative expenses. Direct selling expenses (for example, credit, warranty, and advertising) are expenses that can be directly linked to the sale of specific products. Indirect selling expenses are expenses that cannot be directly linked to the sale of specific products, for example telephone expenses, Internet, and postal charges. General and administrative expenses include salaries of non-sales personnel, rent, utilities, communication, etc.</p></div>

<table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" class="authRefData" style="display: none;" id="defref_us-gaap_StockholdersEquity">
<tr><td class="hide"><a style="color: white;" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.hideAR();">X</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>Total of all stockholders' equity (deficit) items, net of receivables from officers, directors, owners, and affiliates of the entity which are attributable to the parent. The amount of the economic entity's stockholders' equity attributable to the parent excludes the amount of stockholders' equity which is allocable to that ownership interest in subsidiary equity which is not attributable to the parent (noncontrolling interest, minority interest). This excludes temporary equity and is sometimes called permanent equity.</p></div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>The entire disclosure for cash and cash equivalent footnotes,  which may include the types of deposits and money market instruments, applicable carrying amounts, restricted amounts and compensating balance arrangements. Cash and equivalents include: (1) currency on hand (2) demand deposits with banks or financial institutions (3) other kinds of accounts that have the general characteristics of demand deposits (4) short-term, highly liquid investments that are both readily convertible to known amounts of cash and so near their maturity that they present insignificant risk of changes in value because of changes in interest rates. Generally, only investments maturing within three months from the date of acquisition qualify.</p></div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>The entire disclosure for equity method investments and joint ventures. Equity method investments are investments that give the investor the ability to exercise significant influence over the operating and financial policies of an investee. Joint ventures are entities owned and operated by a small group of businesses as a separate and specific business or project for the mutual benefit of the members of the group.</p></div>

</div><div id="a5867" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:52.688px;top:485.1px;">co-venturers do not make necessary equity contributions<div <a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>The entire disclosure for each guarantee obligation, or each group of similar guarantee obligations, including (a) the nature of the guarantee, including its term, how it arose, and the events or circumstances that would require the guarantor to perform under the guarantee; (b) the maximum potential amount of future payments (undiscounted) the guarantor could be required to make under the guarantee; (c) the current carrying amount of the liability, if any, for the guarantor's obligations under the guarantee; and (d) the nature of any recourse provisions under the guarantee, and any assets held either as collateral or by third parties, and any relevant related party disclosure. Excludes disclosures about product warranties.</p></div>

<td class="pl " style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_CommitmentsAndContingenciesDisclosureTextBlock', window );">Contingencies and Commitments</a></td>
<td class="text"><div id="TextBlockContainer44" style="position:relative;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:14.08px;color:#000000;line-height:normal;width:638px;height:387px;display:inline-block;border:inherit;margin-left:-2px;margin-right:-2px;"><div id="a5988" style="position:absolute;font-weight:bold;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:0px;">Note 12&#8212;Contingencies and Commitments</div><div id="a5991" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:262.488px;top:0px;">&#160;</div><div id="a5992" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:16px;">&#160;</div><div id="a5993" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:32.2px;">A number of lawsuits involving a variety of claims<div style="display:inline-block;width:1.94px">&#160;</div>arising in the ordinary course of business<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.17px">&#160;</div>have been filed </div><div id="a5996" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:48.3px;">against ConocoPhillips.<div style="display:inline-block;width:6.24px">&#160;</div>We also may be required to remove or mitigate the effects on the environment of the </div><div id="a5997" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:64.3px;">placement, storage, disposal or release of certain<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.02px">&#160;</div>chemical, mineral and petroleum substances<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.15px">&#160;</div>at various active </div><div id="a5999" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:80.5px;">and inactive sites.<div style="display:inline-block;width:6.55px">&#160;</div>We regularly assess the need for accounting recognition or disclosure of these </div><div id="a6000" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:96.5px;">contingencies.<div style="display:inline-block;width:6.75px">&#160;</div>In the case of all known contingencies (other<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.08px">&#160;</div>than those related to income taxes), we accrue<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.02px">&#160;</div>a </div><div id="a6001" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:112.7px;">liability when the loss is probable and the amount<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.13px">&#160;</div>is reasonably estimable.<div style="display:inline-block;width:6.23px">&#160;</div>If a range of amounts can be </div><div id="a6004" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:128.8px;">reasonably estimated and no amount within the range<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.04px">&#160;</div>is a better estimate than any other amount,<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.14px">&#160;</div>then the low </div><div id="a6006" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:144.8px;">end of the range is accrued.<div style="display:inline-block;width:6.16px">&#160;</div>We do not reduce these liabilities for potential insurance or third-party recoveries.<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.31px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a6012" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:161px;">We accrue receivables for insurance or other third-party recoveries when applicable.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5.59px">&#160;</div>With respect to income </div><div id="a6015" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:177.2px;">tax-related contingencies, we use a cumulative probability-weighted<div style="display:inline-block;width:1.64px">&#160;</div>loss accrual in cases where sustaining a </div><div id="a6022" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:193.2px;">tax position is less than certain. </div><div id="a6024" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:209.3px;">&#160;</div><div id="a6025" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:225.3px;">Based on currently available information, we believe<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.01px">&#160;</div>it is remote that future costs related to known<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.02px">&#160;</div>contingent </div><div id="a6026" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:241.5px;">liability exposures will exceed current accruals by<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.05px">&#160;</div>an amount that would have a material<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.17px">&#160;</div>adverse impact on our </div><div id="a6028" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:257.6px;">consolidated financial statements.<div style="display:inline-block;width:6.07px">&#160;</div>As we learn new facts concerning contingencies,<div style="display:inline-block;width:1.96px">&#160;</div>we reassess our position </div><div id="a6029" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:273.6px;">both with respect to accrued liabilities<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.15px">&#160;</div>and other potential exposures.<div style="display:inline-block;width:6.29px">&#160;</div>Estimates particularly sensitive to future </div><div id="a6030" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:289.8px;">changes include contingent liabilities<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.17px">&#160;</div>recorded for environmental remediation, tax and legal<div style="display:inline-block;width:2px">&#160;</div>matters.<div style="display:inline-block;width:3.2px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a6032" </div><div id="a6824" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:144.8px;">received approximately $</div><div id="a6824_24_3" style="display:inline-block;width:5.42px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a9834" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:128.8px;"><div style="display:inline-block;width:3.52px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a9836" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:145px;">The credit risk from our OTC derivative contracts,<div style="display:inline-block;width:1.93px">&#160;</div>such as forwards, swaps and options, derives<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.11px">&#160;</div>from the </div><div id="a9837" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:161px;">counterparty to the transaction.<div style="display:inline-block;width:6.13px">&#160;</div>Individual counterparty exposure is managed<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.02px">&#160;</div>within predetermined credit </div><div id="a9838" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:177.2px;">limits and includes the use of cash-call margins when appropriate,<div style="display:inline-block;width:1.66px">&#160;</div>thereby reducing the risk of significant </div><div id="a9842" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:193.3px;">nonperformance.<div style="display:inline-block;width:6.62px">&#160;</div>We also use futures, swaps and option contracts that have a negligible credit<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.15px">&#160;</div>risk because </div><div id="a9843" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:209.3px;">these trades are cleared with an exchange clearinghouse<div style="display:inline-block;width:1.8px">&#160;</div>and subject to mandatory margin requirements until </div><div id="a9845" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:225.5px;">settled; however, we are exposed to the credit risk of those exchange<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.15px">&#160;</div>brokers for receivables arising from daily </div><div id="a9846" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:241.6px;">margin cash calls, as well as for cash deposited to meet<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.06px">&#160;</div>initial margin requirements.<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.72px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a9848" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:257.6px;">&#160;</div><div id="a9849" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:273.8px;">Our trade receivables result primarily<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.16px">&#160;</div>from our petroleum operations and reflect a broad<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.1px">&#160;</div>national and </div><div id="a9851" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:289.8px;">international customer base, which limits our<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.16px">&#160;</div>exposure to concentrations of credit risk.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5.62px">&#160;</div>The majority of these </div><div id="a9852" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:306px;">receivables have payment terms of </div><div id="a9852_34_7" style="position:absolute;font-size:14.08px;left:202.613px;top:306px;">30 days</div><div id="a9852_41_59" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:245.813px;top:306px;"><div style="display:inline-block;width:3.52px">&#160;</div>or less, and we continually monitor this exposure<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.06px">&#160;</div>and the </div><div id="a9854" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:322.1px;">creditworthiness of the counterparties.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5.81px">&#160;</div>Our collateral requirements will depend on the<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.07px">&#160;</div>creditworthiness of our </div><div id="a9856" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:338.1px;">counterparties.<div style="display:inline-block;width:6.49px">&#160;</div>At our option, we may require collateral to limit<div style="display:inline-block;width:1.87px">&#160;</div>the exposure to loss including, letters of </div><div id="a9865" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:354.3px;">credit, prepayments and surety bonds, as well as<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.21px">&#160;</div>master netting arrangements to mitigate<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.12px">&#160;</div>credit risk with </div><div id="a9869" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:370.3px;">counterparties that both buy from and sell to<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.14px">&#160;</div>us, as these agreements permit the amounts<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.17px">&#160;</div>owed by us or owed </div><div id="a9870" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:386.5px;">to others to be offset against amounts due to us. </div><div id="a9873" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:402.6px;">&#160;</div><div id="a9874" style="position:absolute;font-size:14.08px;left:4.693px;top:418.6px;">Certain of our derivative instruments contain provisions that require us to post collateral if the derivative </div><div id="a9875" style="position:absolute;font-size:14.08px;left:4.693px;top:434.8px;">exposure exceeds a threshold amount.  We have contracts with fixed threshold amounts and other contracts </div><div id="a9876" style="position:absolute;font-size:14.08px;left:4.693px;top:450.9px;">with variable threshold amounts that are contingent on our credit rating.  The variable threshold amounts </div><div id="a9878" style="position:absolute;font-size:14.08px;left:4.693px;top:466.9px;">typically decline for lower credit ratings, while both the variable and fixed threshold amounts typically revert </div><div id="a9879" style="position:absolute;font-size:14.08px;left:4.693px;top:483.1px;">to zero if we fall below investment grade.  Cash is the primary collateral in all contracts; however, many also </div><div id="a9881" style="position:absolute;font-size:14.08px;left:4.693px;top:499.1px;">permit us to post letters of credit as collateral, such as transactions administered through the New York </div><div id="a9882" style="position:absolute;font-size:14.08px;left:4.693px;top:515.3px;">Mercantile Exchange.</div><div id="a9882_20_1" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:127.568px;top:515.3px;"> </div><div id="a9885" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:531.4px;">&#160;</div><div id="a9886" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:547.4px;">The aggregate fair value of all derivative<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.15px">&#160;</div>instruments with such credit risk-related contingent<div style="display:inline-block;width:2px">&#160;</div>features that were </div><div id="a9889" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:563.6px;">in a liability position on September 30, 2020 and December<div style="display:inline-block;width:1.67px">&#160;</div>31, 2019, was $</div><div id="a9889_74_2" style="position:absolute;font-size:14.08px;left:430.994px;top:563.6px;">20</div><div id="a9889_76_14" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:445.074px;top:563.6px;"><div style="display:inline-block;width:3.52px">&#160;</div>million and $</div><div id="a9889_90_2" style="position:absolute;font-size:14.08px;left:523.315px;top:563.6px;">79</div><div id="a9889_92_10" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:537.235px;top:563.6px;"><div style="display:inline-block;width:3.52px">&#160;</div>million, </div><div id="a9895" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:579.7px;">respectively.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7.61px">&#160;</div>For these instruments, </div><div id="a9895_38_2" style="position:absolute;font-size:14.08px;left:210.454px;top:579.7px;">no</div><div id="a9895_40_71" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:224.534px;top:579.7px;"><div style="display:inline-block;width:3.52px">&#160;</div>collateral was posted as of September 30, 2020<div style="display:inline-block;width:2px">&#160;</div>or December 31, 2019.<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.95px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a9902" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:595.7px;">If our credit rating had been downgraded below<div style="display:inline-block;width:3.52px">&#160;</div>million of additional collateral, either with<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.15px">&#160;</div>cash or letters of credit.</div></div><span></span>

<tr class="ro">
<td class="pl " style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_FairValueDisclosuresTextBlock', window );">Fair Value Measurement</a></td>
<td class="text"><div id="TextBlockContainer108" style="position:relative;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:14.08px;color:#000000;line-height:normal;width:634px;height:264px;display:inline-block;border:inherit;margin-left:-2px;margin-right:-2px;"><div id="a9914" style="position:absolute;font-weight:bold;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:0px;">Note 14&#8212;Fair Value Measurement </div><div id="a9918" style="position:absolute;font-weight:bold;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:16px;">&#160;</div><div id="a9919" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:32.2px;">We carry a portion of our assets and liabilities at fair value measured at the reporting<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.16px">&#160;</div>date using an exit price </div><div id="a9920" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:48.2px;">(i.e., the price that would be received to sell an asset<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.09px">&#160;</div>or paid to transfer a liability) and disclosed<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.13px">&#160;</div>according to </div><div id="a9921" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:64.3px;">the quality of valuation inputs under the following<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.09px">&#160;</div>hierarchy: </div><div id="a9925" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:80.5px;">&#160;</div><div id="a9926" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:28.693px;top:97.6px;">&#9679;</div><div id="a9927" style="position:absolute;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:35.093px;top:97.5px;">&#160;</div><div id="a9928" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:52.688px;top:97.6px;">Level 1: Quoted prices (unadjusted) in an active<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.18px">&#160;</div>market for identical assets or liabilities. </div><div id="a9930" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:28.693px;top:114.6px;">&#9679;</div><div id="a9931" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:52.688px;top:114.6px;">Level 2: Inputs other than quoted prices that<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.13px">&#160;</div>are directly or indirectly observable. </div><div id="a9934" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:28.693px;top:131.7px;">&#9679;</div><div id="a9935" style="position:absolute;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:35.093px;top:131.6px;">&#160;</div><div id="a9936" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:52.688px;top:131.7px;">Level 3: Unobservable inputs that are significant<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.04px">&#160;</div>to the fair value of assets or liabilities. </div><div id="a9939" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:28.693px;top:147.9px;">&#160;</div><div id="a9940" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:166.4px;">The classification hierarchy of an asset or liability<div style="display:inline-block;width:1.95px">&#160;</div>is based on the lowest level of input significant<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.08px">&#160;</div>to its fair </div><div id="a9941" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:182.4px;">value.<div style="display:inline-block;width:6.95px">&#160;</div>Those that are initially classified as Level 3<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.06px">&#160;</div>are subsequently reported as Level 2 when the<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.17px">&#160;</div>fair value </div><div id="a9943" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:198.6px;">derived from unobservable inputs is inconsequential<div style="display:inline-block;width:1.88px">&#160;</div>to the overall fair value, or if corroborated market<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.1px">&#160;</div>data </div><div id="a9944" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:214.7px;">becomes available.<div style="display:inline-block;width:6.49px">&#160;</div>Assets and liabilities initially reported as Level<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.09px">&#160;</div>2 are subsequently reported as Level 3 if </div><div id="a9945" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:230.7px;">corroborated market data is no longer available.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5.71px">&#160;</div>There were no material transfers into or<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.17px">&#160;</div>out of Level 3 during </div><div id="a9949" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:246.9px;">2020 or 2019.</div></div><div id="TextBlockContainer110" style="position:relative;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:14.08px;color:#000000;line-height:normal;width:636px;height:406px;display:inline-block;border:inherit;margin-left:-2px;margin-right:-2px;"><div id="a9952" style="position:absolute;font-weight:bold;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:0px;">Recurring Fair Value Measurement </div><div id="a9954" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:16.2px;">Financial assets and liabilities reported at fair<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.09px">&#160;</div>value on a recurring basis primarily include<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.17px">&#160;</div>our investment in </div><div id="a9988" style="display:inline-block;width:2.1px">&#160;</div>securities classified as available for sale, and </div><div id="a10018" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:4.693px;top:48.3px;">commodity derivatives.<div style="display:inline-block;width:6.25px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a10024" style="display:inline-block;width:2.04px">&#160;</div>on the NYSE, </div><div id="a10120" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:28.693px;top:129.8px;">and our investments in U.S. government obligations<div style="display:inline-block;width:1.93px">&#160;</div>classified<div style="display:inline-block;width:3.18px">&#160;</div>as available for sale debt securities, which </div><div id="a10151" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;left:28.693px;top:145.9px;">are valued using exchange prices. </div><div id="a10161" <tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>The entire disclosure for the fair value of financial instruments (as defined), including financial assets and financial liabilities (collectively, as defined), and the measurements of those instruments as well as disclosures related to the fair value of non-financial assets and liabilities. Such disclosures about the financial instruments, assets, and liabilities would include: (1) the fair value of the required items together with their carrying amounts (as appropriate); (2) for items for which it is not practicable to estimate fair value, disclosure would include: (a) information pertinent to estimating fair value (including, carrying amount, effective interest rate, and maturity, and (b) the reasons why it is not practicable to estimate fair value; (3) significant concentrations of credit risk including: (a) information about the activity, region, or economic characteristics identifying a concentration, (b) the maximum amount of loss the entity is exposed to based on the gross fair value of the related item, (c) policy for requiring collateral or other security and information as to accessing such collateral or security, and (d) the nature and brief description of such collateral or security; (4) quantitative information about market risks and how such risks are managed; (5) for items measured on both a recurring and nonrecurring basis information regarding the inputs used to develop the fair value measurement; and (6) for items presented in the financial statement for which fair value measurement is elected: (a) information necessary to understand the reasons for the election, (b) discussion of the effect of fair value changes on earnings, (c) a description of [similar groups] items for which the election is made and the relation thereof to the balance sheet, the aggregate carrying value of items included in the balance sheet that are not eligible for the election; (7) all other required (as defined) and desired information.</p></div>

<tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>The entire disclosure of revenue from contract with customer to transfer good or service and to transfer nonfinancial asset. Includes, but is not limited to, disaggregation of revenue, credit loss recognized from contract with customer, judgment and change in judgment related to contract with customer, and asset recognized from cost incurred to obtain or fulfill contract with customer. Excludes insurance and lease contracts.</p></div>

<tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>The entire disclosure for reporting segments including data and tables. Reportable segments include those that meet any of the following quantitative thresholds a) it's reported revenue, including sales to external customers and intersegment sales or transfers is 10 percent or more of the combined revenue, internal and external, of all operating segments b) the absolute amount of its reported profit or loss is 10 percent or more of the greater, in absolute amount of 1) the combined reported profit of all operating segments that did not report a loss or 2) the combined reported loss of all operating segments that did report a loss c) its assets are 10 percent or more of the combined assets of all operating segments.</p></div>

<tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>The entire disclosure for income taxes. Disclosures may include net deferred tax liability or asset recognized in an enterprise's statement of financial position, net change during the year in the total valuation allowance, approximate tax effect of each type of temporary difference and carryforward that gives rise to a significant portion of deferred tax liabilities and deferred tax assets, utilization of a tax carryback, and tax uncertainties information.</p></div>

<table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" class="authRefData" style="display: none;" id="defref_us-gaap_ExplorationExpense">
<tr><td class="hide"><a style="color: white;" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.hideAR();">X</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>Exploration expenses (including prospecting) related to oil and gas producing entities and would be included in operating expenses of that entity. Costs incurred in identifying areas that may warrant examination and in examining specific areas that are considered to have prospects of containing oil and gas reserves, including costs of drilling exploratory wells and exploratory-type stratigraphic test wells. Exploration costs may be incurred both before acquiring the related property (sometimes referred to in part as prospecting costs) and after acquiring the property. Principal types of exploration costs, which include depreciation and applicable operating costs of support equipment and facilities and other costs of exploration activities, are: (i) Costs of topographical, geographical and geophysical studies, rights of access to properties to conduct those studies, and salaries and other expenses of geologists, geophysical crews, and others conducting those studies. Collectively, these are sometimes referred to as geological and geophysical or "G&amp;G" costs. (ii) Costs of carrying and retaining undeveloped properties, such as delay rentals, ad valorem taxes on properties, legal costs for title defense, and the maintenance of land and lease records. (iii) Dry hole contributions and bottom hole contributions. (iv) Costs of drilling and equipping exploratory wells. (v) Costs of drilling exploratory-type stratigraphic test wells.</p></div>

<tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>Amount of currency on hand as well as demand deposits with banks or financial institutions. Includes other kinds of accounts that have the general characteristics of demand deposits. Also includes short-term, highly liquid investments that are both readily convertible to known amounts of cash and so near their maturity that they present insignificant risk of changes in value because of changes in interest rates. Excludes cash and cash equivalents within disposal group and discontinued operation.</p></div>

<tr class="re">
<td class="pl " style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_CreditDerivativeRecourseProvisions', window );">Credit Derivative, Recourse Provisions</a></td>
<td class="text">Certain of our derivative instruments contain provisions that require us to post collateral if the derivative exposure exceeds a threshold amount.  We have contracts with fixed threshold amounts and other contracts with variable threshold amounts that are contingent on our credit rating.  The variable threshold amounts typically decline for lower credit ratings, while both the variable and fixed threshold amounts typically revert to zero if we fall below investment grade.  Cash is the primary collateral in all contracts; however, many also permit us to post letters of credit as collateral, such as transactions administered through the New York Mercantile Exchange.<span></span>
</td>
<td class="text">&#160;<span></span>
</td>

<div style="display: none;">
<table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" class="authRefData" style="display: none;" id="defref_us-gaap_NumberOfOperatingSegments">
<tr><td class="hide"><a style="color: white;" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.hideAR();">X</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>Number of operating segments. An operating segment is a component of an enterprise: (a) that engages in business activities from which it may earn revenues and incur expenses (including revenues and expenses relating to transactions with other components of the same enterprise), (b) whose operating results are regularly reviewed by the enterprise's chief operating decision maker to make decisions about resources to be allocated to the segment and assess its performance, and (c) for which discrete financial information is available. An operating segment may engage in business activities for which it has yet to earn revenues, for example, start-up operations may be operating segments before earning revenues.</p></div>
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">+ References</a><div style="display: none;"><p>Reference 1: http://www.xbrl.org/2009/role/commonPracticeRef<br> -Publisher FASB<br> -Name Accounting Standards Codification<br> -Topic 280<br> -SubTopic 10<br> -Section 50<br> -Paragraph 18<br> -URI http://asc.fasb.org/extlink&amp;oid=120311839&amp;loc=d3e8672-108599<br></p></div>
